newsitem.title: POLAND: World Bank lends Poland $67 mln for port project.
newsitem.headline: World Bank lends Poland $67 mln for port project.

text.p: Poland and the World Bank signed a $67 million loan agreement on Monday to modernise the infrastructure at the country's ports.
Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki told reporters at the signing ceremony that the project aimed at improving road access to ports of Gdansk, Gdynia and Szczecin-Swinoujscie, on the Baltic coast.
"The project marks a change in attitutde towards transport in Poland from a purley service role to a commercial and business one," Liberadzki said.

He said the whole project, which included the construction of a brigde over the Vistula river to Gdansk's Northern Port, two bridges near Szczecin as well as road, waterway and embankment modernisation, would cost a total of $145.6 million.
The World Bank credit will be extended in two tranches of $33.5 million and $49.5 million. The rest of the money will come from the Polish budget.
The loan is for 17 years with interest payments, based on LIBOR, postponed for five years.
